Now, if copying fails, the version change simply doesn't start, and an interrupted version change restores the saves on the next launch
  • Restoring from a backup went straight over the build: nobody checked whether the game was running, and a failure midway left the build half old, half new. Now the archive is unpacked separately and swapped in only as a whole
  • Cancelling the download of a single file with ✕ deleted the whole build. Now such a mod is simply marked as failed, and the installation continues
  • After a build's version change, the backup list showed entries that were no longer on disk
  • Cancelling a build installation didn't stop the download: the disk kept filling up for several more minutes, and a folder was left where the cancelled build had been
  • Installing from a .stzhk file couldn't be cancelled at all — the window hung until the very end, and the cancelled build kept downloading
  • Cancelling a paused transfer left it hanging forever
  • Deleting a build didn't stop its repair — the repair kept creating files of the already deleted build
  • A highly compressed archive could fill the entire disk when installing a build
  • A .stzhk file sent by a friend could bring the launcher down by exhausting memory as early as the preview
  • The launcher window popped up over a second running game
  • Video and sound settings overwrote each other when two games were open at once
  • Server monitoring didn't collect metrics — the charts stayed empty
  • The English interface had some Russian buttons, the Russian one had an English “Browse”, and the launcher folder picker had no title at all
  • Tab stopped twice on the same dropdown
  • A VPN card could be copied with the mouse but not with the keyboard
  • Screen readers now name 64 switches and sliders that used to be read as just “switch” — including the delete and edit buttons for groups
  • The “Friends” section and the transfers screen follow the “Interface → Shape and color” setting — previously their colors were hardcoded
  • An expanded room shows exactly how your build differs from your friend's
  • Checking friends for updates no longer recomputes all your builds every five minutes when notifications are off
  • The export preview no longer reads hundreds of build files into memory at once

entry.title: Stuzhik 0.0.14
entry.content:
• A “Security” tab for instances — three independent checks: whether each mod is found on Modrinth and CurseForge by its file, what a mod can do based on references in its code (network, launching programs, file access), and whether the computer has traces of known infections. Nothing is blocked or deleted, and no “safe” verdict is given — the facts are shown, the decision is yours
  • The security check runs by itself — when an instance is first opened and after new mods are installed; the button remains for re-checking. The result is saved, so the tab opens with a ready report right away, and already analyzed mods aren't analyzed again, even in another instance
  • Custom commands around game launch: a pre-launch command, a wrapper command, a post-exit command and your own environment variables — globally and with per-instance overrides. Like in MultiMC and Prism. The commands are not included in any export format and are not sent to friends over the network — they are only copied between your own instances
  • Build export to CurseForge format — previously there were only .stzhk, .mrpack and a plain zip. Mods not installed from CurseForge are matched to their pages there where possible, so they don't go into overrides as whole files
  • Several accounts at once with quick switching — previously there was one sign-in for the whole launcher, and a second one overwrote the first
  • Datapacks — a separate tab with world selection. Datapacks live inside a world, so the world is picked right in the header rather than in filters; the tab is available for both vanilla builds and servers
  • A “+” tile in a group section on Home creates a build right in that group, no need to drag the card afterwards. Also works in the “Ungrouped” section
  • Instances open noticeably faster: tab counters are computed in one go, the mod list doesn't re-read the folder a second time, and scanning the resources folder no longer makes a separate request per file
  • After installing or updating a mod, only that mod is refreshed rather than the whole list — large builds no longer freeze after every install
  • Some icons in the interface weren't drawn at all, and some blocks had a white border instead of a colored one — 236 styling rules didn't make it into the compiled app
  • In the server and client console, selected text “jumped” to the next line: you select a line, a new one arrives — and the wrong one gets copied. The console also stopped redrawing the whole window for every line, and a stream of hundreds of lines at server start no longer freezes the interface
  • The “Element shape” appearance setting only half worked — the sidebar and the details and settings navigation kept their own corner rounding
  • The account row in the sidebar was narrower than the navigation items
  • Tutorial hints slid off the edge of the window and were cut off
  • A pinned dependency version was treated as a problem if the installed version was newer than the pinned one
  • Log analysis parsed very old logs on a par with the latest launch, re-parsed them every time and drew a white border on problem cards instead of a red one
  • Friends in Stuzhik Connect were lost after a launcher restart — the device got a new identifier every time. Discovery settings now apply immediately, not only after a restart
  • The developer console mounted twice when opened and left a background log reader behind

entry.title: Stuzhik 0.0.13
entry.content:
• Sign-in with a Microsoft account — full sign-in with Xbox Live and a Minecraft: Java Edition license check. Previously choosing the account type in settings did nothing
  • Sign-in with Ely.by — login, password and two-factor code; authlib-injector is downloaded and set up automatically
  • Support for Minecraft 1.6.4–1.7.x — a virtual asset tree and extraction of LWJGL native libraries, without which the game wouldn't start
  • Support for Minecraft 1.5.2 and older (Alpha, Beta, early releases) — assets are laid out in the resources folder inside the instance, as these versions expect
  • Forge support for versions before 1.13, including 1.7.10 — installed without running the installer, which on these versions requires a graphical window and has no console mode
  • Protection against the Log4Shell vulnerability for versions 1.7–1.16.5 — official Mojang patches are downloaded and applied automatically at launch
  • Changing the loader on a server instance — Forge, NeoForge, Fabric and Quilt, with cleanup of the previous loader's files; worlds, mods, configs and player lists are left untouched
  • A “Modpack” tab for instances installed from a modpack — checking for new versions, the full list of changes before updating, in-place update, installing another version as a separate instance and comparing with other instances of the same modpack
  • When updating a modpack, it's shown separately which mods the user added themselves (left alone) and which modpack files they changed manually (will be overwritten)
  • Mod collections: automatic detection of the game versions and loaders supported by all mods in the collection at once
  • Mod collections: compatibility details — which mod blocks which version, known incompatibilities between the collection's mods and their dependencies
  • Mod collections: a dependency preview when adding a mod from the catalog and a removal dialog that breaks down the links within the collection
  • Preview of automatic dependency resolution — what exactly will be installed, for which mods and what is blocked by a conflict, with a jump to any mod's card
  • A catalog of all auto-fix types in the log analyzer, with the option to disable a specific type globally
  • A “Not a problem” mark for dependency conflicts — kept between launches; hidden conflicts can be brought back
  • Named settings sync rules — your own path patterns on top of the built-in knowledge base
  • Preview of a friend's modpack contents — the actual mod list with icons and versions before downloading
  • Instance groups are now always-visible sections with card drag-and-drop instead of a filter showing one group at a time
  • An “Open logs folder” button and picking a specific log file right in the log analyzer
  • Checking a mod file by hash and manually marking client mods on a server instance
  • The app no longer freezes when accessing the database
  • Instance cards are no longer recreated when the status changes — icons don't reload, hover state isn't reset
  • The dependencies panel explains what it shows and what to do about each type of problem; the graph got a legend of link types
  • Quick actions in conflicts: “Install the required version” for pinned dependencies and “Disable mod” for incompatible ones
  • Clicking anywhere on a mod row opens its card, not just clicking the name
  • Mod icons and versions in the removal and removal analysis dialogs; a uniform “icon + mod name” look in all lists
  • Resources and shaders: a list/catalog switch on the left, like in the mods tab, with the count in the header
  • Resource packs and shaders added to the folder manually automatically get their real name, version, description and icon
  • Instance memory follows the global settings unless set explicitly — like the player name and JVM arguments
  • A port-in-use check before starting a server — a clear error instead of an instant “crash” a few seconds later
  • Stuzhik Connect settings (concurrent transfer limit, build update notifications) survive a launcher restart
  • File transfers between friends interrupted by a crash resume on the next launch
  • “Helped / didn't help” answers on solutions found online are saved and loaded again when the problem is reopened
  • Confirmation before an auto-fix and a result notification that is visible regardless of how the problem list is scrolled
  • A dependency installation can be rolled back with one click right after it completes
  • A dialog opened over another one now always ends up on top
  • Old error reports are cleaned up automatically at startup — the folder no longer grows forever
  • When changing a server's loader, the full list of Forge and NeoForge versions is available, not just the latest
  • Performance analysis in logs is noticeably faster on large files
  • The launch button didn't change state: after clicking it stayed “Start” and active until the game actually started
  • NeoForge 20.5 and newer mods weren't recognized anywhere — the platform renamed the mod descriptor file, and the launcher couldn't find it
  • An endless install-and-remove loop when a required dependency is incompatible with an already installed mod
  • The trigger label was missing on all automatic backups — only “Manual” was shown
  • Mod names in crash log analysis turned into fragments like “-1” or “uleLayer”
  • Wrong word form in relative time in Russian: «6 дня назад» instead of «6 дней назад»
  • Pinging a friend almost always timed out — the packet went to the wrong port
  • Window control buttons became unreachable in a narrow window — the title bar was cut off
  • Search in the file viewer didn't find files outside the open folder
  • Release dates in the changelog showed a made-up day of the month
  • “Known conflicts” in a mod card looked like the mod conflicting with itself — now the reason is shown and you can open the other mod
  • An “unknown special query” error when opening the Recipe Builder without a search query
  • Untranslated English text in dependency conflict descriptions
  • Error messages weren't shown when Modrinth or CurseForge was unavailable — the button simply did nothing
  • A NeoForge server could fail to start — the loader was detected as regular Forge
  • Replay protection in file transfers between friends let the very first message of a session through
  • Several places where a file name from a platform response or an archive was inserted into a path without checking
  • The “Removal Analysis” dialog opened pressed into a corner of the screen and showed “1 mods”
  • File list rows ran together: path, size and time overlapped
  • Error reports were removed only from the window; the files on disk stayed forever
  • App crash on specially crafted data from a platform or another user
  • Instance installation steps didn't advance — the indicator showed “Java” as active throughout the installation, although the line below it was already reporting loader work
  • Overlapping text in the server and client console when the game writes long lines one after another
  • The “Mods” tab showed the “no mods” block twice

entry.title: Stuzhik 0.0.12
entry.content:
• Before installing a mod from the catalog — a preview of which other mods will be installed automatically (required dependencies) and which can be added if you like (optional), with a warning about incompatibility with mods already installed
  • When removing a mod — a warning about which other mods will break or lose features, and optional cleanup of the removed mod's own orphaned dependencies
  • Detection of conflicts with specific versions of mod dependencies, not just version ranges
  • “Keep original” when converting a client to a server — a separate copy is created instead of irreversibly changing the original instance
  • Preview of modpack sync with a friend — how many files will be downloaded and deleted, without an actual transfer
  • Quick version bump (+Patch/+Minor/+Major) when exporting a modpack
  • Instance groups are stored in the database rather than in localStorage — they survive a launcher reinstall
  • Mod checks after a folder sync cover only the changed mods rather than all of them at once — noticeably faster for large builds
  • A custom Java path in settings is validated right when it's added, not only when it's used
  • A hint about what exactly the automatic firewall setup will do is shown before you press the button
  • TPS in the server console is more accurate and has no warm-up delay — it's queried directly via RCON
  • The “Dependencies” tab in a mod card updates when you pick another version in the version list
  • The settings sync dialog shows a preview of the contents by category right after you choose the source instance
  • Dropdowns appeared offset for a moment when opening and “jumped” into place
  • Server and client console lines overlapped each other during a stream of logs
  • The resource and shader count badge didn't update on removal, only when you re-entered the instance
  • The sidebar could stay expanded when navigating via the ⌘K palette or a tutorial step rather than by clicking the sidebar itself
  • The interface could briefly freeze when opening the “Installed” tab in Resources and Shaders, during backups, in the log analyzer, when importing from other launchers and during operations on instance files
  • The “Play” button in Quick Play didn't show launch status — it looked like nothing was happening
  • Duplicate resource pack and shader entries when scanning the folder — each showed up twice in the list
  • A WebView memory leak when switching animated backgrounds or in interface settings
  • The mod version list and update suggestions sometimes showed a file name instead of the version number; updating some mods failed with an error
  • A mod's publish and update dates in the catalog and the mod card were always empty
  • The mod auto-update setting had no effect — new mods from the catalog always got auto-update regardless of it
  • CurseForge catalog pagination didn't go past the first page
  • Bulk mod removal didn't check dependent mods after removal, unlike removing a single mod
  • The banner about known mod conflicts (e.g., OptiFine and Iris) wasn't shown on the mod card
  • Launching with a missing required mod dependency reported nothing — the crash happened inside the game with no explanation
  • Minimum memory (-Xms) for server instances was ignored at launch — only the maximum was used
  • The “Apply fix” button (increase memory) in the Performance panel didn't work
  • Automatic switching to ZGC on newer Java was disabled if a specific Java path was chosen in the instance settings instead of “Automatic”
  • A freshly created server instance with the Vanilla, Fabric or Quilt loader couldn't find its JAR at launch
  • The run.bat and run.sh scripts from the Forge and NeoForge installers lacked nogui — starting the server manually opened an extra window
  • Importing a NeoForge instance from another launcher detected the loader as regular Forge
  • A patch dragged into the launcher window was handled as a modpack — patches now have their own extension, and dragging the file in opens the apply-patch dialog
  • A patch created from a modpack comparison didn't include config changes
  • A mod's side and whether it is required couldn't be edited in the modpack editor — only viewed
  • Optional mod groups (mutually exclusive choice) weren't shown in the modpack editor
  • Importing an existing .mrpack archive as a new modpack editor project — there was no button
  • The order of mods in a modpack editor project couldn't be changed
  • Checking an instance's files against the manifest of the original .stzhk it was installed from — wasn't in the interface
  • The history of patches already applied to an instance wasn't shown
  • Test-launching a modpack right from the editor — there was no button
  • You couldn't ban a player or an IP address — only unban and kick
  • The Spark profiler buttons always failed with an error, even while the server was running
  • Server metrics (CPU, memory, TPS in the console) were never collected
  • Links to past Spark reports could only be found in the in-game chat
  • Manually checking client mods on a server instance — wasn't in the interface
  • The “Import” button in the log analyzer didn't work
  • Searching online for solutions to a problem found in the log analyzer — there was no button
  • Picking a specific instance log file for analysis — only via the system file picker
  • Deleting an error report removed it only from memory — the file on disk stayed forever
  • The network and firewall diagnostics panel had disappeared from Stuzhik Connect
  • The automatic firewall setup button configured nothing — it only opened the OS settings for manual setup
  • The reverse server → client conversion wasn't in the context menu
  • Importing from a launcher installed in a non-standard folder — you couldn't specify the path manually
  • You couldn't add a peer's modpack to the Stuzhik Connect transfer queue, change the priority of a pending item or clear the whole queue
  • Selective sync (e.g., only mods without resource packs) had no effect on the actual file transfer, even when turned on
  • Friend ping, groups on a friend's card and the update-watching status weren't in the interface
  • Protection against path spoofing when installing mods with a forged file name and when restoring instance backups
  • News content is now safely sanitized before display, like the rest of the text in the app
  • Parts of the interface stayed in Russian when another language was selected

entry.title: Stuzhik 0.0.11
entry.content:
• Watch Mode — automatic sync with a friend when build files change (a new “Watch Mode” tab in Stuzhik Connect)
  • The P2P transfer speed limit can be set in the interface
  • Friend groups, editing a friend's nickname and notes about them
  • RCON: Kick and Say buttons right in the server console, a list of online players
  • Duplicate an instance with one click
  • Checking and restoring the integrity of instance files
  • Resource packs and shaders caught up with the mod list in features — update checks, bulk actions, export
  • Download mirror management in settings
  • Spark profiler buttons right in the interface instead of instructions in chat
  • Highlighting of the launcher's own news tab and a badge when there's something new
  • RCON moderation (whitelist/ban/op) applies immediately to a running server, not only after a restart
  • Trust between friends now syncs correctly
  • Protection against path spoofing when receiving files from a friend
  • The integrity manifest updates itself after regular actions with mods and configs, not only manually
  • Additional context menu items for instances; right-click on a profile tab
  • Faster resource checks; duplicating an instance no longer leaves a partial copy on error
  • Launching on Windows failed with an error when the user name contained Cyrillic characters
  • Running two instances of the same Minecraft version at once caused an instant crash
  • The launcher's first start could end with a database error
  • The server port set when creating an instance wasn't applied
  • Converting a client to a server didn't install the server JAR
  • Inviting a friend to a server failed with a “P2P not initialized” error, even when P2P was working
  • The button for syncing a modpack with a friend in Stuzhik Connect did nothing — no files were transferred
  • The transfer “History” and “Queue” sections in Stuzhik Connect were in the interface but always stayed empty
  • Notifications about a friend's modpack update were in the interface (badge, list) but never arrived
  • Memory slider — wrong value step
  • The sidebar got stuck open
  • Mod version card — a crash and a wrong “installed” status
  • The Play/Stop button got stuck if stopping the instance failed
  • Crash analysis was duplicated; crash history wasn't always recorded
  • False warnings about missing fabric-api
  • A mod's icon disappeared after installing, updating or changing its version
  • Resource packs and shaders couldn't be reused across instances
  • Automatic dependency lookup always went to Modrinth, even for CurseForge mods
  • Selective modpack import ignored excluded mods and overrides
